title: Python foundations: safe failures and object invariants

turns.message: I’ll guess: safe_divide should catch every exception and return None, because callers should never see an error.
I’m stuck; which invalid BankAccount operation must leave the balance unchanged?
Correct answer: catch only ZeroDivisionError for the documented zero denominator; unrelated errors should propagate.
The invariant is non-negative balance, and failed withdrawals or non-positive deposits must not mutate it.
/verify Rectangle.__init__ raises ValueError before storing a negative dimension.

expectations.notes: Teach narrow exception boundaries and constructor validation before the object challenge; identify state preservation after a failed operation; distinguish rejected construction from later mutation.
